{{Draft}}
<translate>
<!--T:1-->
Every statement in a catalogue raisonné should be traceable: which book gives this catalogue number, who measured this work, where does this date come from? openCR records this with '''sources''' and '''citations''', the footnotes of the online catalogue.

<!--T:2-->
* A '''source''' is where information comes from: a publication, a letter, an expert report, an interview, a conversation with the artist, a website. It is entered once and reused wherever it is cited, in any catalogue.
* A '''citation''' links a record, or one field of it, to a source, together with the place in the source: "this date comes from that letter, page 2".

<!--T:3-->
A record or a field can have any number of citations.

<!--T:4-->
== Sources ==
A source is not a reference typed out as text. It is stored as separate fields, and openCR composes its title from them in the reader's language. The same letter appears as
* ''Letter from A to B, Paris, 12 March 1974'' in English,
* ''Brief von A an B, Paris, 12. März 1974'' in German,
* ''Carta de A a B, Paris, 12 de marzo de 1974'' in Spanish.

<!--T:5-->
The type, the roles, the country and the date are translated; names, the city and the original title are shown as entered.

<!--T:6-->
A source has the following fields. Which of them the form offers depends on the type.
{| class="wikitable"
! Field !! Content
|-
| '''Type''' || What kind of source it is; see [[#Source types|Source types]]. Required.
|-
| '''People''' || One line per role of the type, for example ''Sender'' and ''Recipient'' of a letter. Each person is a [[Directory|directory]] entry or an [[Artists|artist]], found with ''Search name''. When nobody can say who it was, choose '''Unknown''': the examiner unknown, the owner unknown.
|-
| '''Date''' || Day, month and year, each of them optional, with a qualifier such as ''approximate''. Types that cover a period have ''Date (from)'' and ''Date (to)''.
|-
| '''City''', '''Country''' || Where the source was written, issued or kept.
|-
| '''Language''' || The language of the source.
|-
| '''Reference number''' || A file, certificate or invoice number, or an archive's shelfmark.
|-
| '''Web address''', '''Accessed on''' || For websites: the address and the day it was consulted. Both are required.
|-
| '''Original title''' || The source's own title, as written, if it has one.
|-
| '''Description''' || A short description, one text per interface language.
|-
| '''Label in lists''' || The name under which editors find the source when they search. Left empty, it is made from the title.
|-
| '''Public''' || Whether visitors see the source; see [[#Who sees what|Who sees what]].
|}

<!--T:7-->
A source of the type ''Publication'' only names a [[Publications|publication]] of the bibliography, found by its title. Its title is the publication's title and year; the authors and all other details are in the bibliography.

<!--T:8-->
=== Source types ===
Each type has its own roles. A role marked ''required'' must name a person or be set to ''Unknown''. Every type except ''Publication'' has a date; "date from–to" marks the types that cover a period.
{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Roles !! Further fields
|-
| '''Publication''' || — || the publication
|-
| '''Letter / correspondence''' || Sender (required), Recipient (required) || date from–to, city and country, language, reference number
|-
| '''E-mail''' || Sender (required), Recipient (required) || date, language
|-
| '''Certificate''' || Issuer (required), Recipient || date, city and country, reference number
|-
| '''Invoice / delivery note''' || Issuer (required), Recipient || date, reference number
|-
| '''Manuscript / notes / diary''' || Author (required) || date from–to, language, reference number, original title
|-
| '''Expert report''' || Examiner (required) || date, language, reference number, original title
|-
| '''Archive file''' || Holding archive (required) || date from–to, city and country, reference number (the shelfmark), original title
|-
| '''Interview''' || Interviewee (required), Interviewer || date, city and country, language
|-
| '''Personal communication''' || Informant (required), Recipient || date
|-
| '''Physical inspection''' || Examiner (required) || date, city and country
|-
| '''Film / video''' || Director, Producer || date from–to, language, reference number, original title
|-
| '''Photograph (as evidence)''' || Photographer || date, city and country, reference number
|-
| '''Website''' || Author, Publisher || date, web address and date accessed (required), language, original title
|-
| '''Supplied material''' || Supplier (required), Recipient || date
|-
| '''Other document''' || Author, Issuer || date from–to, city and country, language, reference number, original title
|}

<!--T:9-->
=== Choosing the type ===
* Information given in conversation, by telephone or informally, for example by the artist, an heir, an owner or a dealer, is a '''Personal communication''' with that person as ''Informant''.
* An examination of the work itself, for example to measure it, is a '''Physical inspection'''. A written opinion by an expert is an '''Expert report'''.
* Photographs, scans or documents that someone passed on to you are '''Supplied material''', with that person or institution as ''Supplier''.
* Printed and published works belong in the bibliography: enter them as [[Publications|publications]] and cite them with a source of the type '''Publication'''. Unpublished letters, e-mails, certificates, invoices, manuscripts and diaries are sources of their own type, not publications.
* Use '''Other document''' only when no other type fits.

<!--T:10-->
=== Who may create and change sources ===
Any editor can create a source. It is saved at once (''Save source and use it'' in the citation pop-up, ''Save source'' in image uploads), independently of the record being edited, and from then on it can be cited in any catalogue. A source can be changed only by the editor who created it and by the platform administrator.

<!--T:11-->
Scans or photographs of a source, such as a letter or a certificate, are added on the source's page with ''Add scans'', by those who may change the source.

<!--T:12-->
== Citations ==
A citation connects a record, or one of its fields, to a source. It has:
{| class="wikitable"
! Field !! Content
|-
| '''Field''' || The field the citation supports, or ''Whole record''.
|-
| '''Source''' || An existing source, found by its label, or a new one. Before anything is typed, the list offers the sources already cited in the artist's catalogue.
|-
| '''Where in the source''' || Any number of locators, each a kind and a value; see below.
|-
| '''Quote''' || The passage that supports the value, word for word, in the language of the source, with its ''Language of the quote''. Quotes are never translated.
|-
| '''Comment''' || A remark on the citation, one text per interface language: for example why the source is doubted, or how a value was derived from it.
|-
| '''Public''' || Whether visitors see this citation.
|}

<!--T:13-->
Whoever may edit a record may add, change and remove its citations. The citations of a measurement follow its artwork, those of an address its directory entry, those of a relation either of the two entries it connects, and those of an alternative name its artist. The citations of a source can be changed by those who may change the source.

<!--T:14-->
=== Where in the source ===
''Add page, figure …'' adds a locator. Its value is free text of up to 50 characters, such as ''14'', ''12–14'' or ''00:03:20''. The abbreviation is put in front of it in the reader's language: ''p. 14'', ''S. 14'', ''pág. 14''.
{| class="wikitable"
! Locator !! English !! German !! Spanish
|-
| Page || p. || S. || pág.
|-
| Volume || vol. || Bd. || vol.
|-
| Figure || fig. || Abb. || fig.
|-
| Plate || pl. || Taf. || lám.
|-
| Catalogue number || no. || Nr. || n.º
|-
| Folio || fol. || fol. || fol.
|-
| Sheet || sheet || Bl. || h.
|-
| Timecode || colspan="3" | (no abbreviation)
|-
| Item || item || Pos. || part.
|}

<!--T:15-->
=== Adding citations ===
Citations are added on the page of the record itself, in the editors' view (''Edit Mode''): the page of an artwork, an artist, a directory entry, an event, a publication or a source. The buttons appear for those who may edit the record.
* ''Add source'', a small book with a plus sign after a value, cites that value. Measurements, addresses, relations and alternative names shown on the page have a button of their own.
* ''Add source for the whole record'', under '''Sources''' at the bottom of the page, cites the record as a whole.
* ''Edit'' and ''Remove'' are in the box that lists a value's sources and in the ''Sources'' list at the bottom of the page. ''Remove'' asks for confirmation.
Each button opens the '''citation pop-up'''. ''Save'' stores the citation straight away, on its own, and the page reloads to show it; ''Cancel'' closes the pop-up without saving.

<!--T:21-->
In the pop-up:
* '''Field''' appears only when the button stands for several fields, such as the date, place and country of creation: choose the one the source supports.
* '''Source''': under the list of types, the search box and ''New source'', the pop-up offers three of the sources already cited in the artist's catalogue (for a record without an artist, cited anywhere), as ''Recently used'', ''Most used'' or ''Recently created''; ''Recently created'' takes the newest sources of all. Choosing a type in place of ''All types'' narrows the offer to that type; typing searches all sources by their label in lists. Click a source to choose it; ''Change'' goes back to the list.
* '''New source''' turns the pop-up into the source form. ''Save source and use it'' saves the source and returns to the citation with the source chosen; ''Back'' returns without it. A chosen source that you may change has ''Edit source''.
* The other fields, from ''Where in the source'' to ''Public'', are described under [[#Citations|Citations]].

<!--T:16-->
Two other places attach sources:
* '''Uploading images''': ''Mass New Objects Upload'' and the upload of a single image have the optional field ''Source of these images''. Every image of the upload gets a citation to that source, which records where the files came from. This is not the photographer, who is credited on the image itself.
* '''Copying an artwork''': with ''Copy sources'' (ticked by default), every copied section keeps the citations of its original.

<!--T:17-->
== Reading sources ==
* A value with sources has a small book icon after it, with the number of its citations when there are several. Point at it to see the titles of its sources. Click or tap it, or move to it with the keyboard and press Enter, and a box lists them: the title of each source with the place in it (''p. 14'', ''no. 25''), the quote in its original language, and the comment. Escape, a click elsewhere or the box's close button closes it.
* Each title is a link. A ''Publication'' source opens the page of the publication. Any other source opens its own '''source page''': type, people (linked to their directory or artist pages), date, place, language, original title, reference number, web address and description, and the records that cite it (''Cited in … records'').
* At the bottom of the page, '''Sources''' counts the citations, for example ''3 sources (2 on fields, 1 on the whole record)'', and lists those of the record as a whole, followed by any citation of a field the page does not show.
* Pages of artworks, directory entries, publications, events, artists and sources show markers in the same way, for example at titles, names, dates, addresses and relations; each measurement of an artwork has its own.
* The switch '''Accessible view''' at the top of the page puts words next to the icons, makes the buttons larger and writes the sources out under their value instead of in a box. The browser remembers the setting.

<!--T:18-->
=== Who sees what ===
Visitors see a citation only when both the citation and its source are ''Public''. In the editors' view all citations are shown, and those hidden from visitors are marked ''(not public)''.

<!--T:19-->
== The former data source field ==
Until October 2026, artworks and their measurements had a single field ''Data source type'', with a ''Data source''. Sources and citations have replaced it. Its values became citations of the record as a whole:
* a publication (a catalogue raisonné, literature): a ''Publication'' source, with the artwork's ''Internal reference'' as the ''catalogue number'' where the work had one;
* the artist, the heirs, a publisher or an owner: a ''Personal communication'' with that person as ''Informant'';
* a physical examination: a ''Physical inspection''.
Where the old data named no person, the informant or examiner is ''Unknown''. If you know who it was, tell the platform administrator, who can complete the source.

</translate>
